what_this_is: Every parameter the sweep passes to the geometry whose value does NOT vary across the
sweep. If a number reaches an OpenSCAD module as a named argument and is the same on
all 132 buildable variants, it is a setting, and it belongs here rather than in Python.
These are not axes. The axes live in variant_param/*.csv and are combined factorially,
so a column added there multiplies the variant count; the values below are the same on
every variant by design, and changing one moves the whole sweep together.
The membership test is mechanical, not a matter of taste: resolve the Parameters tree
for every variant in all three families, collect what each numeric field actually takes,
and keep the fields that come back with exactly one value. That is how boom_tolerance
and cowl_flange_tolerance were found -- neither sits near the others in the source, and
neither is named like a setting at its definition site.
The coefficients inside the derivation formulas are here too, in 'standard' and
'scaling'. They do not reach geometry as values -- the sweep passes what they produce --
but they are design parameters all the same, and leaving them as bare numbers mid-
function is how the reciprocal pair in panel_offset (0.25 and 4) and eleven
nominal/floor pairs came to be written twice each with nothing tying them together.
Naming did NOT restructure the arithmetic. Each literal was replaced in place, keeping
the operation order, because floating-point multiplication is not associative and
rewriting max(2*sqrt(U)*w, 2*w) as 2*w*max(sqrt(U),1) can move the last bit. The one
exception is the quantum, where q*ceil(x/q) replaces 0.25*ceil(4*x): both operands are
powers of two so the result is bit-identical, and it collapses a reciprocal pair that
silently rounds wrong if only one half is edited.
Read by fuselage_variants.load_constants(). Every key below is required and no other key
is accepted -- a typo is an error rather than a silently ignored row, and a value the
sweep needs can never go missing and be replaced by a default.
Changing a value re-renders on the next --resume: these reach the generated part
definitions by value, and that is what the staleness comparison reads.

tolerances._about: Clearances between mating parts, measured against the parameterization the SWEEP actually uses -- extrusion_width 0.6, not the 0.4 the hand drivers carry. A positive value is spacing that is MEANT to be there: it accommodates manufacturing variation and adhesive bond thickness, so a joint built with no gap has nowhere for the bond to go and nothing to absorb print variation. A NEGATIVE value is an interference fit and is equally legitimate for a printed joint -- FDM parts carry enough dimensional spread that a nominal interference is often how a fit is made to grip, and tightening rather than loosening is a design choice. Negatives were refused here until 2026-08-18 on the assumption that none of these joints was an interference; nose_flange_tolerance is the counter-example that removed the rule.

longeron_tolerance.why: Clearance on the longeron tube in the corner's bore and in the chamfer that leads into it.

greeble_tolerance.why: The snap-fit clearance between the bulkhead's greeble post and the corner's socket. Carried entirely on the CORNER -- its bore is opened out by this much and the bulkhead's post stays nominal, so the joint takes the clearance once. There is deliberately no bulkhead counterpart; 'the post is nominal' is an invariant, not a setting.

corner_tolerance.why: Clearance on the two corner faces that seat against the bulkhead -- the flat at flat_x and the diagonal -- over the corner's full height. Carried entirely on the corner, same as the greeble: when the bulkhead re-evaluates that shape to cut its own socket it passes 0. Held at 0 because 0 is what every flown part was built at. OPEN: if these faces are bonded, 0 leaves no bond line.

panel_tolerance.why: The gap the panel stands off the flange face by, so its outer surface still lands flush with the mold line at corner_radius. Applies only where there IS a panel: a cowling bulkhead and the 0 mm panel variants take 0, and that zero is structural rather than a setting -- no panel, no gap to leave.

boom_tolerance.why: Clearance on the boom tube in the boom bulkhead's collet: collet_radius = boom_diameter/2 + boom_collet_thickness + boom_tolerance. Four times the longeron's 0.05 and nothing on record says why -- the boom is a larger tube through a deeper bore, but the number has never been justified in writing.

cowl_flange_tolerance.why: Clearance between the bulkhead's cowl-mounting flange and the cowl that slides over it. Sets the flange's outer radius at corner_radius - cowl_n_perimeters*extrusion_width - cowl_flange_tolerance: the perimeter term is the radial room the COWL's wall occupies, so the cowl's outer surface still lands on the mold line. Applies only to a cowling bulkhead; every other type takes 0, and that zero is structural -- there is no cowl flange on a bulkhead that mounts no cowl.

nose_flange_tolerance.why: Fit between the nose cowl's base flange and what it seats into. Sets the base offset at cowl_n_perimeters*extrusion_width + nose_flange_tolerance, so the flange is inset from the OML by the cowl's own wall thickness plus this. NEGATIVE, and deliberately: at the sweep's extrusion_width of 0.6 and one perimeter, 0.6 + -0.1 = 0.5, which is the inset the nose cowl has always been built with. Written down this way it is a 0.1 mm interference -- a joint that grips rather than one that is bonded. It was previously the bare literal 0.5, which only decomposes tidily as 0.4 + 0.1 against the hand drivers' extrusion width; that 0.4 is not the parameterization the sweep runs, so reading the value through it was reading it through a nozzle nothing uses. This value changes NO geometry.

geometry._about: Shape of the part rather than fit between parts. Constant across the sweep for the same reason the tolerances are -- nothing derives them from size -- but they are not clearances and are not subject to the non-negative rule.

greeble_opening_angle.why: Half-angle of the wedge cut out of the greeble, so the mouth is 70 degrees wide. That mouth is what makes the greeble a C rather than a closed ring, and it is how the longeron is assembled: the tube presses in sideways and snaps into the bore, which the chord across the mouth (2*r*sin35 = 57% of the tube diameter) is narrow enough to hold. Arrived at by experiment -- a tuned value, not a derived one. Do not replace it with a formula.

boom_key_angle.why: Rotation of the anti-rotation key around the boom tube, in degrees. The upper and lower webs mirror it as 180 - boom_key_angle, so 0 puts the key on the fuselage centerline. Never anything but 0 in the sweep; it exists because the key does not have to be there.

standard._about: The parametric standard: what 1U means, in millimeters. scaled_standard_values() multiplies each by U (and unit_length by FX as well) and everything else is derived from the result. These are the numbers a fuselage IS. Refused if not strictly positive.

unit_width.why: Across-flats width of the fuselage box at 1U. Also the datum the boom bulkhead's y and z positions are expressed as fractions of.

unit_length.why: Bay length at 1U and FX=1. The only standard value FX scales, because FX is the bay-length axis and nothing else responds to it.

corner_radius.why: Radius of the rounded corner at 1U -- the mold line the panel's outer surface is flush with, and the outer radius of the corner extrusion.

longeron_radius.why: Radius of the longeron tube at 1U. The corner's bore is this plus longeron_tolerance.

bolt_offset.why: Distance from the corner arc center to the bolt axis at 1U.

scaling._about: Coefficients inside the derivation formulas. Three units are mixed here and the suffix says which: _extrusions is a count of extrusion_width, _layers a count of layer_height, _per_u a multiple of U in millimeters, and a bare _mm is an absolute floor that does not scale. Where a formula floors a scaled value at its own coefficient -- max(3*U, 3) -- one name now appears on both sides, which is the point: they were two independent literals that had to agree and nothing said so. Refused if negative.

greeble_wall_extrusions.why: Greeble wall thickness, as max(n*sqrt(U)*extrusion_width, n*extrusion_width). sqrt(U) not U: the wall is a printed feature sized to survive a snap fit, so it scales in extrusions rather than as a fraction of the airframe. The floor is the same n because a one-extrusion wall has no interior.

panel_overlap_min_mm.why: Floor on panel overlap, as max(panel_thickness, this). Absolute millimeters and deliberately unscaled -- it is a bond-area minimum, not a proportion of the airframe.

greeble_margin_extrusions.why: Clearance beyond the greeble's outer wall, in extrusions, keeping the panel's inner corner off the greeble perimeter. Appears three times in one derivation and is one quantity in all three: it is added into panel_clearance_radius, then removed before that radius is projected onto the 45-degree diagonal, then added back after. Splitting it into three names would let the projection stop undoing what it was meant to undo.

greeble_snap_clearance_per_u.why: Extra width around the greeble so the corner can snap in from the back side.

panel_offset_quantum_mm.why: Panel offset is rounded UP to a whole multiple of this, as q*ceil(offset/q). Was written 0.25*ceil(4*offset) -- the same parameter as its own reciprocal, two literals that had to stay inverse and nothing said so; editing one alone rounds to a grid nobody chose.

cowl_flange_height_per_u.why: Height the cowl-mounting flange stands off the bulkhead face. Zero on any bulkhead that mounts no cowl, which is structural rather than this value set to nothing.

cowl_bulkhead_flange_extrusions.why: Bulkhead flange wall on a COWLING bulkhead, as max(ceil(n*U)*extrusion_width, n*extrusion_width). One extrusion thicker than the frame bulkhead's, because it carries the cowl.

bulkhead_flange_extrusions.why: Bulkhead flange wall on every non-cowling bulkhead, same form as above.

bolt_thickness_per_u.why: Boss thickness around the bolt, as max(n*U, n) -- so it never falls below its own 1U value on a sub-unit airframe.

plate_layers.why: Plate thickness as ceil(n*U) whole layer heights. A count of layers, not a length: the plate is a printed skin and wants to come out an exact number of passes.

web_fillet_radius_per_u.why: Fillet where the web meets the bulkhead ring.

boom_web_width_per_u.why: Web width on a boom bulkhead -- twice the frame bulkhead's, because the web carries the boom.

frame_web_width_per_u.why: Web width on every non-boom bulkhead.

bulkhead_flange_fillet_per_u.why: Fillet at the root of the bulkhead flange.

bulkhead_flange_chamfer_per_u.why: Chamfer on the leading edge of the bulkhead flange.

boom_wall_per_u.why: Wall thickness of the boom bulkhead itself.

boom_collet_thickness_per_u.why: Wall of the collet that grips the boom tube. The bore is boom_diameter/2 + this + boom_tolerance.

boom_key_width_per_u.why: Width of the anti-rotation key, as max(n*U, n). Equal to the key height today; named separately because they are independent dimensions that happen to agree, and merging them would make one impossible to change.

boom_key_height_per_u.why: Height of the anti-rotation key, as max(n*U, n). See the note on the key width.

boom_key_radius_per_u.why: Corner radius on the key, as max(n*U, n).

boom_key_web_width_per_u.why: Width of the web that carries the key.

printer._about: Properties of the machine, not of the design. The same airframe printed on a different nozzle wants different numbers here and no other change. Refused if not strictly positive.

extrusion_width.why: Nozzle width the sweep sizes printed features against -- the greeble wall, the bulkhead flange and the cowl flange are all whole multiples of it. Was written out seven separate times across three files, each overriding a PrinterSettings default of 0.4 that nothing wanted; the default now comes from here and the overrides are gone. The hand drivers in scad/ are still at 0.4 and that is deliberate, not drift.

layer_height.why: Layer height the sweep sizes printed features against. Only plate_thickness = ceil(4*U) * layer_height reads it today. Unlike extrusion_width this was never overridden anywhere -- it sat as a dataclass default -- so the two halves of one machine profile were configured in opposite ways.

slicing._about: How a part is SLICED, which is neither a property of the machine nor of the design. Separate from 'printer' deliberately: the same nozzle prints a vase-mode cowl at one perimeter and a solid corner at several, so a perimeter count cannot live beside extrusion_width without claiming to be a machine setting. Per part, because parts are sliced independently and nothing requires a corner's count to match a cowl's. Refused if not a positive whole number. Decided in OQ-DES-CW9.

cowl_n_perimeters.why: How many perimeters a COWL is printed with. 1 is spiral vase mode, which these cowls support and which OQ-DES-CW6 decided to keep -- but vase is not the only way they can be printed, so this is a stated configuration rather than a property of the part. Three dimensions are functions of it, and in all three it is the COWL's count even where the geometry belongs to another part: the rib thickness 2*w*n + t_cut (OQ-DES-CW3), the cowling bulkhead's flange radius, which leaves this much radial room for the cowl wall so the cowl's outer surface lands on the mold line, and the nose cowl's base offset. Change it and the mating bulkhead must be rebuilt with it: at 0.6 mm extrusion width, printing a cowl at 3 perimeters against a flange cut for 1 is 1.2 mm of interference.
